provenance.title: CUSP SHAPE AND TUNNEL NUMBER
provenance.authors: VINH DANG AND JESSICA S. PURCELL

candidates.statement: By the 6-Theorem [2, 23], the cusp shapes of these manifolds must lie in a bounded region of the moduli space of the torus.

Thus while the shortest slope of the torus must have length at least one, and therefore long narrow tori have at most one exceptional Dehn ﬁlling, we cannot determine whether fatter tori are large or small, with long or short slope lengths.

To ﬁnd such a structure on C(1; 2), a choice of three appropriate curves on ∂+C(1; 2) must be pinched, which amounts to ﬁnding values of ρ(α), ρ(β) and ρ(γ1) for which certain products of generators have trace ±2, namely those products that represent the boundary curves.
Since there are no hyperbolic manifolds with smaller genus Heegaard splittings, M must have tunnel number one. □ Corollary 5.1.
candidates.section_title: Cusp shapes of tunnel number n manifolds
